audit.whatIsWrong: The content level chart gives Tahm Kench 5 of 7 stages and Trundle none, while Trundle wins 55.38% of 186 games. The full layer for the same matchup reads Trundle / Skill / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench / Trundle / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench, and the mirror page (champ-data/content/tahmkench.js, a=tahmkench b=trundle) carries that identical seven-stage chart.
audit.why: Two layers of the same matchup contradict each other, and the content one is the outlier. Trundle owns level 1 outright — Chomp is a 3.5s auto-reset that saps AD before Tahm Kench has learned Thick Skin — and owns level 6 outright once Subjugate exists. Handing those two stages to Tahm Kench is the single biggest thing wrong with the page.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Trundle, Level 2 Skill, Level 6 Trundle — matching the full layer and the mirror exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] credits Trinity Force with duelling him "through his W devour-then-spit pattern". Devour is the ultimate; Abyssal Dive is the W. spikes[3] says Subjugate "strips half his resistances" and stops there.
audit.why: The late-game spike is understated by the part it omits. Subjugate takes 40% of current armour and MR AND 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as damage, healing Trundle for the same amount. Against the champion whose entire build is health, the health component is the spike, not the resist steal.
audit.corrected: First item: Trinity Force Spellblade off every Chomp auto-reset. Late: Subjugate scales off the health and resists he buys — his Heartsteel stacks are your ultimate's scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seven fields call Tahm Kench's grey health a "passive": spikes[0], wants.foe[2], early, mid, whys[0], whys[3], whys[4] all say "grey-health passive".
audit.why: The passive is An Acquired Taste — bonus damage from total health, and the stack counter that gates Devour. Grey health is Thick Skin (E), a 3-second-cooldown active that converts stored damage into a shield. The distinction is the whole early lane: Thick Skin is a button he has to press and a spell he has to have learned, so it does not exist at level 1 and it has a window between casts. Calling it a passive tells the player it is always on and there is nothing to play around.
audit.corrected: Grey health is Thick Skin (E), 3s cooldown, an active. An Acquired Taste is the passive and it is the stun/Devour counter.

audit.whatIsWrong: Abyssal Dive is described everywhere as an escape: full tldr, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns ("His escape + shield"), dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, loading, content mid ("that is his only clean out") and wants.foe[1] ("Use Abyssal Dive to escape the Frozen Domain zone").
audit.why: Abyssal Dive is a channelled engage on 21/20/19/18/17s that knocks up on landing, and it is not a shield at all — the shield is Thick Skin. A Trundle who builds his whole gameplan around waiting for Tahm Kench's 'escape' is tracking the wrong button, and a Tahm Kench reading the mirror is being told to channel out of a fight he is losing.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (21/20/19/18/17s, 1000-1200 range) is a telegraphed channelled engage with a knockup. The button that actually threatens you is Devour, and it needs three An Acquired Taste stacks first.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states the actual escape hatch from the matchup's kill pattern: An Acquired Taste stacks decay, and Devour cannot be cast until the target carries three of them.
audit.why: Every death in this lane is the same sequence — two stacks land, the third arrives with Tongue Lash and stuns, then Devour. Breaking contact after the second stack removes the ultimate from the matchup entirely. That is the single most actionable fact on the page and it is absent.
audit.corrected: Leave after the second An Acquired Taste stack. Devour needs three, and so does the Tongue Lash stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] says Subjugate drains "half his armor and MR", spikes[1] says "drain his Armor and MR", spikes[3] says "strips half his resistances", wants.you[2] says "the drained Armor and MR". None of the four mentions the health component.
audit.why: Subjugate steals 40% of current armour and MR, deals 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as magic damage, and heals Trundle for that same amount — half immediately, half over 4 seconds. Against Tahm Kench the health line is the bigger half of the ability by a distance.
audit.corrected: 40% of his armour and MR plus 20-30% of his max health as damage and the same again as healing, doubling over 4 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: sequencingCues 0, no cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer. "Track Abyssal Dive before every commit" is stated four times without a figure.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and it is the stack engine, Abyssal Dive is 21/20/19/18/17s, Thick Skin is a flat 3s, Chomp is a flat 3.5s and Pillar of Ice is 21s at rank 1. Those numbers turn vague respect into a rule: bite, leave on the second stack, and step back in when Tongue Lash has missed.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2].why, report[5].t, early and wants.you[1].

audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for Tongue Lash and Thick Skin, and report[8] already prescribes Executioner's Calling on first back at roughly 800g. That is the right call and the right timing, so I left itemization alone.

The packet's only suspectName here, "Use Abyssal Dive" in wants.foe[1], is a false positive on the NAME — Abyssal Dive is spelled correctly. The sentence is still wrong, but for the reason in point 4, not a misnaming.

edits.before: Tahm Kench's grey-health passive is the problem in the first three levels — every Chomp you land converts to a HP buffer he gets to keep, so trades that look like wins on your screen feel like draws on his. Respect Tongue Lash completely: he needs three Tongue Lash hits to stack his passive stun, and standing still in auto range gives him those stacks free. Stay mobile, Chomp only when moving, and farm with Pillar if he tries to zone you off the wave. You are not winning these levels outright; you are surviving them at acceptable HP to reach 6.
edits.after: Thick Skin, not his passive, is the problem from level 3 — every Chomp you land is stored and cashed back as a shield on a 3-second cooldown, so trades that look like wins on your screen feel like draws on his. Level 1 is still yours: Chomp is a 3.5s auto-reset that saps his AD before Thick Skin is even learned. After that, respect Tongue Lash — 7s at rank 1, and each hit is an An Acquired Taste stack. Break contact on the second: the third one stuns, and Devour cannot be cast until it lands.

edits.before: At 6 the matchup flips on its axis. Tahm Kench's identity is a tank, and Subjugate is the hardest anti-tank tool in the entire top-lane roster — hit R the moment the duel opens and you are literally wearing his armor and MR for the fight. Drop Frozen Domain at your feet, Chomp to steal his AD, auto-weave inside the zone for the attack speed boost, and Pillar behind him to deny Abyssal Dive escape. His grey-health passive still slows the kill, but the stat drain tilts the duel too far in your favor for him to survive a full pattern. Track Abyssal Dive before every commit — that is his only clean out.
edits.after: At 6 the matchup flips on its axis. Tahm Kench's identity is health and resistances, and Subjugate is the hardest anti-tank tool in top lane — hit R as the duel opens and you take 40% of his armour and MR plus a fifth of his max health, healing yourself the same. Drop Frozen Domain at your feet, Chomp to steal his AD, auto-weave in the zone for the attack speed, and Pillar of Ice behind him so he has to walk out the long way. Thick Skin slows the kill, but the stat swing is too big for him to survive a full pattern. Count his An Acquired Taste stacks the whole time — Devour needs three, so break contact on the second.

edits.before: Late game Tahm Kench doubles down on his tank itemization, which is exactly where you want him — every armor and MR item he buys becomes your armor and MR the instant Subjugate lands in a team fight. Split-push inside Frozen Domain where Abyssal Dive is irrelevant to escape distance, and always target their tankiest frontliner in 5v5 fights with R. The 55% win rate is built here: you lose the lane phase and still win the game because his identity feeds your ultimate's payoff. Never fight him without Subjugate available and never burn R on a carry when their tank is alive.
edits.after: Late game Tahm Kench doubles down on his tank itemization, which is exactly where you want him — every armour, MR and health item he buys makes Subjugate bigger, because it takes 40% of his resists and a fifth of his max health and hands you both. Split-push inside Frozen Domain, and always target their tankiest frontliner in 5v5 fights with R. The 55% win rate is built here: you lose the middle of the lane and still win the game because his identity feeds your ultimate's payoff. Never fight without Subjugate up, and never burn R on a carry while their tank lives.

notes: Chart disagreement I did NOT propagate: the mirror and the full layer both give Tahm Kench the First-item and 2+-items stages, while the content layer says Skill. Trundle wins 55.38% here and Subjugate scales off exactly the health-and-resist build Tahm Kench commits to after two items, so writing 'Tahm Kench wins 2+ items' would be inventing a power shift I believe is false. I left win[5] and win[6] alone; mirror-fix.js will flag it. See questionsForUser. The 'grey-health passive' misattribution looks templated — it appears in Trundle's Tahm Kench entry seven times and is worth a sweep across every champion's tahmkench entry. Pillar of Ice terrain duration: the tahmkench__trundle mirror states 6 seconds; the kit file gives no duration and I could not verify it, so I kept the number out of every line I wrote rather than contradict the mirror.
